name: Base-model translation to English before the fine-tuned formalizer (Romanian and mixed messages)
registered_by: translate-eval-agent (owner question of 2026-09-29, relayed by the orchestrator: CPU-only evaluation; no training, no GPU)
frozen_before_results: Written after the translation prompt and the language detector were chosen on the formalizer-v1 development split only (24-row translation pilot, detector checked on all 5,131 dev rows) and before any translator or translated prediction touched a sealed suite (formalizer-v1 test, formalizer-ood-v1, formalizer-wild-v1). Any later change is a recorded deviation.
kind: evaluation-only (CPU inference with existing checkpoints and unmodified base models; no optimizer step, no training data change)
question: Do the small fine-tuned formalizers do better on Romanian and mixed messages when the host first translates the message into English with an original (base, not fine-tuned) instruct model?
owner_scope_correction: 2026-09-29T10:55Z: the translators are the ORIGINAL base versions of the models we fine-tuned. Qwen3-0.6B is out of scope (never fine-tuned); a Qwen GGUF was converted and a server started but no Qwen output was produced on any sealed or dev row, and it was deleted.

hypotheses.H1: On formalizer-ood-v1 RO+mixed rows, SmolLM2-360M (fv1-size-a4, Q8_0) reaches higher tolerant execution equivalence on the Gemma-translated message (T1) than on the message as written (T0).
hypotheses.H2: The same holds on the 400-row stratified RO+mixed sample of the formalizer-v1 sealed test and for the wild accepted-gold match (secondary).
hypotheses.H3: Translation preserves the proper names the target keeps as written (name fidelity of the translation >= 0.90).

changed_factor: The single message given to the formalizer: as written (T0) or the output of a base translator (T1, T2). Formalizer weights, quantization, runtime, decoding and scoring are identical to formalizer-size-v1.

translators.T0: identity (no translation): the existing formalizer-size-v1 Q8_0 predictions, reused; SmolLM2-360M on the formalizer-v1 sample has only a 500-row stratified sample, so T0 is predicted again for the 400-row sample (overlap with sample500 reported as a rerun control).

T1.why: multilingual (Gemma 3 covers 140+ languages); the most likely small model to translate Romanian

T2.why: the owner asked for the original base models; SmolLM2 is English-centric (its pretraining mix is essentially English), so its Romanian translation quality is expected to be poor and is reported as measured

translators.T3_optional: SmolLM2-135M-Instruct base @12fd25f7 (models/smollm2-135m/translator-base/q8_0.gguf, sha256 f38145e7...), only if time allows; SmolLM2 is English-centric, same caveat as T2
translators.excluded: Qwen3-0.6B (owner correction: not one of our fine-tuned models)

T4.runtime: transformers in localhost/chatsop-spark-training:cu130-20260927, CPU 8 threads, no network

prompts.p2: Translate this Romanian text to English. Keep names, numbers, dates and quoted text unchanged. Reply with the English text only.\n\n{message}
prompts.p3: {message}\n\nTranslate the text above into English. Keep proper names, numbers, dates and quoted text exactly as written. Write only the translation.
prompts.selection: Dev pilot of 24 RO/mixed formalizer-v1 dev rows (seed 1): share of Romanian-detected messages that come out detected as English. Gemma p1 2/20, p2 11/20, p3 16/20; SmolLM2-360M base p1 12/20, p2 18/20, p3 15/20. The pilot already showed frequent meaning changes, answers instead of translations and refusals for both models.
prompts.decoding: one user turn, chat template of the model (--jinja), temperature 0, top_k 1, max_tokens min(2048, ceil(chars/2)+64)
prompts.cleanup: trim; strip a leading 'Here is the English translation...:', 'English translation:', 'Translation:' or 'English:'; strip surrounding double quotes when the original was not quoted; an empty output falls back to the original message

routing.label: primary: rows whose label is Romanian or mixed (row language ro, or code_switch true, or wild language mixed) are translated; all rows in scope are such rows
routing.detector: variant: lower-case words with Romanian diacritics count 2, Romanian closed-class words count 1; route when Romanian evidence >= 2 and >= half the English closed-class words. Dev split: routes 93.3% of RO, 64.5% of mixed and 1.2% of EN rows. A row in scope the detector misses keeps its T0 prediction. EN false positives are reported as a rate only (their translated predictions are not produced).

formalizers.runtime: llama.cpp 99d4026b llama-server -ngl 0 -t 8 -tb 8 -np 4 -c 32768 --jinja, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty; one server at a time (8 threads total); harness tools/research/predict-endpoint.mjs, message as the only user turn, temperature 0, top_k 1, max_tokens 6144, parallel 4

formalizer-v1.sampling: stratified proportional sample of the 2,498 RO+mixed rows by (language slice, base language), seed 42, mulberry32 shuffle (predict-endpoint.mjs sampleRows): ro 281, ro code-switched 65, en code-switched 54

metrics.primary: Paired delta (T1 minus T0) of tolerant execution equivalence (DS016) for SmolLM2-360M on formalizer-ood-v1 RO+mixed rows.
secondary: the same for T2 and for SmolLM2-135M; per slice (ro, mixed), long/short, detector routed/missed
formalizer-v1 sample: tolerant execution equivalence, canonical match, parse
wild: accepted-gold match, decision match, shape match, proposition F1, parse; reference-free metrics (eval/run.mjs --messages) against the ORIGINAL messages

name fidelity: gold role values containing a capital letter that occur verbatim in the original message (first accepted target on wild): share present in the translation, in the T0 SOP and in the translated SOP
latency: translation per message (p50/p95/mean) and end-to-end mean translation + formalization against the direct formalization, measured at 4 parallel slots on 8 threads
metrics.uncertainty: 95% paired cluster bootstrap (clusters = semantic_case_id, row id on wild; 10,000 resamples, seed 7) and exact McNemar on rows (tools/research/spellfix-eval.mjs bootstrap/mcnemar).

decision_rule: Recommend a host translation pre-step with translator T only if, for SmolLM2-360M: (a) the OOD RO+mixed delta is positive with a 95% interval excluding 0; (b) the formalizer-v1 sample delta and the wild accepted-match delta are not significantly negative (upper bound >= 0); (c) translation name fidelity >= 0.90; and (d) the end-to-end mean latency is at most 3x the direct one. Any significantly negative primary delta means 'harmful, do not adopt'; otherwise 'no measurable benefit, do not adopt'.
limitations_declared: The targets keep proper names and titles as written (for example 'Grădina Botanică din Timișoara'), so any translation of a name makes a correct formalization impossible: the design penalizes translators that translate names, which is the host's real constraint.

The formalizers were fine-tuned on Romanian messages with canonical English targets; a translated message is an English message, a distribution the formalizers know well, but translation errors are not recoverable.
Translator prompts were chosen on a 24-row dev pilot; no translator was tuned.
Latency is measured with 4 parallel slots on 8 shared threads while the owner uses the chat server; it is a relative, not absolute, figure.
Single seed, greedy decoding, experiment-grade, no human review.

budget.priority_if_short: OOD RO+mixed with SmolLM2-360M and T1 first

deviations.what: The formalizer-size-v1 T0 run of SmolLM2-360M on the formalizer-v1 sample ran concurrently with other CPU load (load average up to 15); SmolLM2-360M T2 formalization had 3 OOD and 1 formalizer-v1 request timeouts (300 s), counted as empty predictions.
deviations.effect: Latency figures only; timeouts are failures in the translated condition (at most 4 rows).

deviations.what: Owner decision (relayed by the orchestrator): stop using the base small LLMs (T1 Gemma 3 270M-it, T2 SmolLM2-360M-Instruct) as translators because they cannot translate. Completed: T1 and T2 with the SmolLM2-360M formalizer on all three suites. Not run: the SmolLM2-135M formalizer arm (stopped at its first suite, no output kept) and the optional SmolLM2-135M base translator.
deviations.effect: Secondary arms dropped; the primary comparison (SmolLM2-360M, T1) is complete.

deviations.what: Owner addition: T4 = Opus-MT, a dedicated MarianMT RO->EN model, as the only translator from here on. Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-ro-en does not exist on the Hugging Face hub (HTTP 401/not found on 2026-09-29); the Romance->English model Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-roa-en @c26705dd (Apache-2.0; source languages include ron; card BLEU ron->eng Tatoeba 55.2, newstest2016 35.8) is used instead, unmodified, greedy (num_beams 1), each message split into sentences on [.!?] + whitespace, sentences translated independently and joined with a space; no prompt. Code: training/python/translate_marian.py run in the training image with no network.
deviations.effect: New translator condition T4, evaluated under the same scorers, comparator and decision rule as T1/T2.

deviations.what: Owner asked for GPU bulk inference; the local permission system refused GPU access (a training job owns the GPU), so T4 translation and all formalization stay on the CPU (8 threads), as in the original request.
deviations.effect: Wall time only; every number records device cpu.

deviations.what: Owner rule (sequential stopping, added before any T4 sealed-row output): T4 is evaluated in nested stratified stages (100, then 300, then all rows; tools/research/translate-eval.mjs stage, seed 42) on each suite in scope. After each stage the paired delta and its 95% cluster-bootstrap CI are computed on the primary endpoint (SmolLM2-360M, OOD tolerant execution equivalence). Stop when (a) the CI excludes 0 in either direction by a margin of at least 2 points (bound beyond +2 or below -2 points), (b) futility: the CI upper bound is below +1 point, or (c) the condition is broken: parse failures or empty outputs above 20% on the first 100 rows. The full set runs only when the result is still ambiguous. The same stages are run on the formalizer-v1 sample and wild as secondary endpoints and stop with the primary.
deviations.effect: T4 may be decided on a stratified subset; the stage and reason are recorded here.

deviations.what: Sequential stop. T4 formalizer-v1 sample stopped at stage 100 (delta -25.0 points [-37.4, -12.0], harm beyond 2 points). T4 OOD and wild ran stage 300 (OOD 0.0 [-5.6, +5.7], still ambiguous; wild accepted match +2.7 [+0.7, +5.0]) and were then stopped by owner decision D1 (the small model no longer translates; the host translates normalized content words with dictionaries), which settles the question. Full sets not run.
deviations.effect: T4 conclusions rest on stratified stage samples of 300 (OOD, wild) and 100 (formalizer-v1).
